label: Aristotle's contextual truth/being correspondence supports a stronger Thomistic biconditional
note: Metaphysics II.1, 993b24–31, gives a correspondence between each thing's standing in being and truth after an argument about eternal principles and their caused truths. It does not say that Aquinas's truth-of-things conformity to an originating intellect (TRUE_3) holds, nor spell out the global pairwise 'if and only if' comparisons over arbitrary beings and respects encoded by 5a948c37. Applying those to all beings and identifying TRUE_7 with TRUE_3 are separate unverified analyst commitments. This relation supplies contextual support only; it is not a historical stating claim or a verified bridge.
